subject: general
question: Our solar system is a part of which galaxy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Milky Way**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Our planetary system is located in an outer spiral of the **Milky Way galaxy**.
 
• Our solar system consists of **stars**, the **Sun**, and everything bound to it by gravity – the **planets** are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, Pluto the **dwarf** **planet**, dozens of moons, millions of asteroids, comets, and, meteoroids.
 
• Scientists have discovered thousands of planetary systems orbiting other stars in the Milky Way.
 
• The **Milky Way** is the galaxy that includes our Solar System, a **hazy band **of light seen in the night sky formed from stars that cannot be individually distinguished by the naked eye.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Messier 81 (also known as **Bode's Galaxy**) is a grand spiral galaxy about 12 million light-years away, with a diameter of 90,000 light years, in the constellation Ursa Major. 
 
• The** Triangulum Galaxy** is a spiral galaxy 2.73 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Triangulum. It is catalogued as Messier 33 or NGC 598.
 
• The **Andromeda Galaxy**, also known as Messier 31, M31, or NGC 224 and originally the Andromeda Nebula, is a barred spiral galaxy with a diameter of about 46.56 kiloparsecs approximately 2.5 million light-years from Earth and the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way.
